objective: Determine whether the proposed workflow solves a recurring problem that target users would allocate budget to solve before authorizing product construction.
target_roles: Utility large-load planning or economic-development representative
Infrastructure-focused real estate or development advisor
questions: In the last 12 months, how often have you compared candidate sites using power availability, interconnection timing, permitting/zoning, and infrastructure constraints?
What parts of that process consume the most staff or consultant time?
What tools, spreadsheets, consultants, utility contacts, or internal systems do you use today?
What errors, delays, duplicated work, or missed information create the most cost or risk?
Would a source-linked comparison packet that organizes these inputs before engineering/legal/utility review save meaningful time? Why or why not?
Who owns budget for this work and how is it currently paid for?
What would have to be true before you would pay for a tool or service like this?
At what price would a single-project or monthly version become obviously too expensive to consider?
What capability would make this immediately useful, and what capability would make you reject it?

success_thresholds.recurring_problem: At least 2 of 3 qualified respondents report the workflow occurs repeatedly or consumes material project time.
success_thresholds.clear_cost_or_delay: At least 2 respondents identify a concrete labor, consultant, delay, or coordination cost.
success_thresholds.budget_signal: At least 1 qualified respondent identifies a real budget owner or current paid substitute.
success_thresholds.willingness_to_pay: At least 1 unrelated qualified respondent gives a credible positive purchase/test signal at a stated price or agrees to a paid pilot.
success_thresholds.scope_fit: No majority requirement for autonomous engineering, legal determinations, utility approvals, or other prohibited high-consequence decisions.

failure_conditions: Respondents describe the problem as rare or trivial.
Existing tools already solve the bounded workflow with little friction.
Value depends primarily on proprietary data JakeAI cannot lawfully or economically access.
Buyers require regulated engineering or legal conclusions rather than evidence preparation.
No qualified respondent identifies budget, cost, or willingness to pay.

routing.PASS: Send evidence to Build Authorization Gate; construction still remains disabled until technical/security/legal review requirements are attached.
routing.HOLD: Refine scope or gather additional buyer evidence without building the full product.
routing.REJECT: Archive candidate unless materially new buyer evidence appears.

notes: Public market research may support problem existence, but it does not count as willingness-to-pay validation. Responses should be attributable to a real qualified role while respecting privacy and permission requirements.
